scope_summary: pydumpling/snapshot/values.py bounded capture walk (value, _mapping, copies, key selection, memo) as an optional PyO3 abi3 extension; pure-Python walk kept as reference and fallback

story.headline: A 7x faster capture walk that never runs your code
story.intro: I ported pydumpling's bounded capture walk, the part of a crash dump that copies every frame's variables while the failing process waits, to a PyO3 extension in 100% safe Rust. The pure-Python walk stays the reference and the fallback, and the native walk must produce byte-identical snapshots.
story.ch1_narrative: Discovery: profiling showed the value walk dominates bounded capture, at 1-3 us of interpreted dispatch per node. The rest of the project (writer, debugger, report, CLI) is I/O bound or built on pdb, so I scoped the port to values.py and the context helpers it calls, 567 lines of Python, rather than replacing a pure-Python wheel with per-platform builds for no gain.
story.ch2_narrative: Blueprint: the contract is strict. Capture never runs application code, and memo order, node counts and truncation counters are all part of the pickled snapshot. I designed the walker as a transaction: wherever the Python walk would call application code, or its result would depend on the recursion limit, the walker rolls back and hands the whole call to Python before anything runs.
story.ch3_narrative: Rewrite: 17 modules, 3,530 lines of Rust code and 877 of comments, none over 400 lines, no unsafe. A descriptor binds ctx.value to the walker without adding a Python frame; an insertion-ordered memo with an undo journal stands in for ctx.objects and ctx._sources, which the walker writes lazily, only when Python code could read them; per-type facts from the MRO are read once per call instead of once per value; and a native finalizer writes what the walker still holds before the cyclic collector frees a context.
story.ch4_narrative: Verification: twenty-two adversarial reviews broke my assumptions. The first found code run twice and crashes on small thread stacks; the second a dropped walker that never flushed its memo and a depth check that audit hooks defeated; later ones found hooks the walker could not see, copy protocols it bypassed, Python code that edits the memo dicts between calls in ways the counts did not show, a context the cyclic collector freed before its walker wrote, and writes that failed halfway or met keys whose comparison runs code. Every code finding became a regression test, and more than 60 fixes were reverted one at a time to check that a test fails without them; the two that no test caught at first got new tests. Not every difference could be closed: the ones left, such as a RecursionError a few levels earlier near CPython's C recursion limit, are documented in the blueprint. The final sweep: 30,000 parity seeds, byte-identical but for those documented differences.
story.ch5_narrative: Optimization: across six workloads, the first native build with PGO took capture from 73.2 ms to 9.3 ms (7.88x) and save_dumping from 96.4 ms to 33.1 ms (2.91x). The checks the reviews added cost about 7% of capture, leaving the current build 7.3x faster than the original Python walk on capture and 3.0x on save (sums; 3.4x and 2.1x geomean against the current Python walk), with byte-identical snapshots. A memo hit costs about 1.1 us natively against 0.05 us in Python, and a new context that captures a single int about 5.5 us against 2.5 us, so a throwaway context capturing a scalar is faster in Python; with a 20-key dict it is 7.9 us against 19.8 us. Containers are where the walker wins.

opportunities.title: Value walk dominates bounded capture
opportunities.description: ValuesMixin.value/_mapping pay 1-3 us of interpreted dispatch per node; the bounded capture time is mostly this walk. Ported to a PyO3 walker that mirrors it step for step.

opportunities.title: Unlimited mode re-serializes subtrees on the way down
opportunities.description: values.py:251 probes every value with dill.dumps (context.py:214-225) before descending; a deep chain ending in one unserializable leaf costs O(depth^2) serialization. Not changed: unlimited snapshots stay on the Python walk.

opportunities.title: _namespaces may hold the id of a freed temporary dict
opportunities.description: _attribute_mapping (values.py:143-156) registers id() of a filtered temporary dict; _mapping frees it unremembered only when the node budget is exhausted, after which nothing else is captured, so the stale id is never read. Benign; documented, not changed.

opportunities.title: Native recursion would use the C stack
opportunities.description: Python 3.12+ frames live on the heap but a Rust walk recurses on the C stack. The walker bounds native stack to 256 KiB and the Python recursion margin, then hands the whole call back to the Python walk from a rolled-back state.

opportunities.title: Dispatch without an extra Python frame or a reference cycle
opportunities.description: Instance-attribute dispatch broke throwaway contexts (context freed mid-call); a strong walker->context ref would form a GC-only cycle keeping originals alive. A class-level native descriptor returns a short-lived bound call instead.

opportunities.title: Hashable dict subclass copies break set capture
opportunities.description: A set member that is a hashable dict subclass is copied to a FakeDict (unhashable), so captured.add(converted) raises TypeError and the whole capture of the set fails; user-visible as a lost variable.

opportunities.title: Non-dict mappings are read through their own items()
opportunities.description: _mapping calls source.items() for any non-dict namespace (exec/class-body locals, mappingproxy of custom mappings) up to three times; a one-shot generator view loses later passes' entries, and key ids are not kept alive between passes.

opportunities.title: _root_value rollback misses _nodes and _truncation
opportunities.description: After a RecursionError in a frame variable, _root_value forgets the half-built copies but keeps their node count and truncation counters, so budgets are spent on discarded work.

opportunities.title: SimpleNamespace and module attributes are dropped
opportunities.description: _attributes only trusts a getset __dict__ descriptor; types whose instance dict is exposed through a member descriptor (SimpleNamespace, modules) are captured without their attributes.

opportunities.title: First capture mutates an exception's __dict__
opportunities.description: Reducing an exception materializes its lazily created __dict__, so the first capture changes the object and every later capture differs.

opportunities.title: str-subclass __qualname__ runs application code
opportunities.description: _type_name concatenates module + '.' + name; a str-subclass __qualname__ runs its own __radd__ and slicing during capture.

opportunities.title: Exception messages embed per-run addresses on 3.15
opportunities.description: Python 3.15 renders an over-long int's repr as a placeholder with its address, so a message built from captured args differs between two dumps of the same state.

test_iterations.failures_summary: pytest (native): 10 of 276 failed with ReferenceError 'the snapshot context is gone'. Throwaway contexts (SnapshotContext(o).value(x)) were freed while the weakly referenced walker ran. Rust: 5 unit, 1 doc, 0 proptest yet.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Replaced per-instance weakref dispatch with a class-level native descriptor (Dispatch.__get__) returning a short-lived BoundValue/BoundMapping that holds the context only during the call: no ctx<->walker cycle, no extra Python frame.

test_iterations.failures_summary: pytest native 276/276 and PYDUMPLING_NATIVE=0 276/276; cargo test 5 unit + 1 doctest + 2048-case Memo proptest pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

No test failures, but the safe_rust benchmark showed b2_heavy_nolimits peak RSS 335 MB vs 72 MB legacy: phys_footprint grew ~4.5 MB per capture with malloc in-use and pymalloc arenas flat. vmmap: 'Malloc Large (empty)'. MallocLargeCache=0 made it flat; a diagnostic allocator replacing realloc with alloc+copy+free made it flat: macOS never reuses large blocks freed by realloc chains (memo entries, Chosen.entries). Also found fresh attribute-name strings kept by CPython's type cache.
test_iterations.fix_applied: memo::push grows a full Vec into a fresh buffer (alloc+free) instead of realloc; used for the memo and key selection. Attribute names interned. Footprint now flat at 46 MB over 25 captures (pure 48.6 MB). Totals: 597 pytest native + 6 cargo tests + 3 clippy-clean targets.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Adversarial review (4 lenses, reproduced) found: SIGBUS on small thread stacks (native recursion bounded only by a fixed 256 KiB budget); hand-backs replaying application code (own items(), str-subclass __qualname__, hostile class dicts) so hooks ran twice; stale cached type facts after __bases__ changes; hidden 3.13 __init__ shim frames under-counted near the limit; 3.11 C-call recursion accounting; process-global statics breaking reload/vendoring; class-level calls, mocks and subclass overrides bypassed; odd argument shapes; empty non-singleton bytes. First run of the new regression tests: 2 failures (copy.copy memo aliasing and str-subclass **kwargs names, both documented as accepted differences); on 3.15 the parity generator built unhashable frozendict keys and exception messages embedded int-repr addresses.
test_iterations.fix_applied: New contract: the native walk never runs application code; it rolls back and hands the whole call to Python before any would run, so hooks run exactly once. stacker::remaining_stack caps the stack budget; depth counted as 2x visible frames; native only on 3.12+ (abi3-py312 and a values.py gate); statics built per values-module import (Statics pyclass from globals()); type facts recomputed per call; Dispatch returns itself on class access and routes ctx-first calls; BoundCall behaves like a bound method; subclasses overriding walk methods keep the Python walk; __getstate__ exports the memo; arguments outside the exact shapes callers pass go to Python as passed; build_native.py finds the artifact via cargo JSON and replaces atomically. 22 new targeted tests; 3.15 harness fixes.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Second adversarial review (api-lifecycle, robustness, app-code, parity reproducers): a dropped walker never flushed its memo (getrefcount from Rust has no temporary reference, so the shared check was off by one); a walker moved to another context lost unwritten copies; bound ctx.value.__doc__ showed PyO3's generated class text signature; full memo export cost 30-125 ms per hand-back; the start check cost 27 us from a 20,000-frame stack; plus audit-hook denial, unreproducible context state, colliding instance-dict keys, planted getsets and surrogate keyword names. Coverage run: two depth-sensitive tests handed back on the unoptimized build's larger frames.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Recursion headroom measured by recursing into values._headroom (capped 1024-frame look); incremental memo mirroring (mirror.rs) flushed before hand-back, __getstate__, retire, release and context switch; retire for state only Python reproduces; real MethodType binding with text_signature=None; Drop compares refcount with a walker-only baseline; 34 new regression tests (re-entry, other-thread error, in-place placeholder replacement, mutation-checked). Final: 736 native + 276 pure pytest + 9 Rust tests on 3.13; 3.14 737; 3.15 737 + 1 environmental (task_for_pid denied). Coverage of the extension from the Python suites: lines 96.3%, functions 96.8%, regions 88.2% (logged; stable rustc has no branch coverage).

test_iterations.failures_summary: Seventh adversarial review confirmed: a removal inside a hand-back masked by that walk's additions (both dicts), a removed _sources original kept alive by the memo, a _walker slot flushing on release, copy hooks the check missed (instance attributes, metaclass __copy__/__getattr__/__getattribute__, class __getattr__, __getnewargs_ex__/__getnewargs__), a colliding _truncation key whose __eq__ ran before a helper, an order-dependent release test and an outcome comparison blind to exception args and subclass items. After the fixes: pytest 943 passed, 2 skipped (3.13); 3.12 943, 3.14 944, 3.11 pure 293; 3.15 944 with the pre-existing macOS sys.remote_exec PermissionError; cargo 9 tests; 13/13 reverted fixes caught.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Boundary check of the last mirrored key in each dict at a hand-back resync and in eager mode; rebuild on a shorter _sources at sync and flush; _walker slot no longer stock; copy-hook names on instance and metaclass (with plain-key guard) checked per call; _truncation keys must be plain; release test on a fresh class first made in either walk, with slots; _comparable reads args, members and subclass items.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Eighth adversarial review (BLUEPRINT: decisions the ninth review forced) confirmed: a flush (copy, pickle, __getstate__, hand-back, retire, release) that checked counts only and wrote back an entry Python removed while adding more; the sync checking where Python left the dicts only during a hand-back or after a copy; a _sources key of another kind whose __eq__ a rebuild ran; copy.replace/__replace__ missing from the copy hooks (dataclass contexts on 3.13+); and a hooks test that could not see metaclass reads. A new differential fuzzer that mixes removals and additions between calls (padding _sources so the count changes) then found the walker's unwritten copies written after Python's additions once Python removed an entry, also when it removed the entry the walker wrote last and put it back, or added an objects key that is not an id. After the fixes: pytest 994 passed, 2 skipped (3.13); 3.12 991, 3.14 995, 3.11 pure 293; 3.15 995 with the pre-existing macOS sys.remote_exec PermissionError; cargo 9 tests; 13/13 reverted fixes caught.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Every flush but a commit's checks the key ending each mirrored part; the sync checks it whenever a count changed; after a removal the walker finds where Python's additions begin from the entry it wrote last (by key identity in _sources, by id in objects) or the first key it does not know; a _sources key not of a plain kind sends the context to the Python walk and pruning reads keys in order; __replace__ joins values._COPY_PROTOCOL and the metaclass names; 30 new parity tests.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Ninth adversarial review (BLUEPRINT: decisions the tenth review forced) confirmed: a removal with as many additions between calls went unnoticed before any copy, so once a flush checked where Python left the dicts a later one put Python's addition after the walker's next copies; after a removal the walker took Python's additions to begin after its last entry wherever that was, so the entry put back after an addition (objects, or the same _sources key) put the walker's copy after both; and copy.replace through a __class__ property or class attribute missed the copy hooks. The fuzzer, no longer padding _sources, then found an original the walker wrote that Python put into a replaced _sources counted as the walker's. After the fixes: pytest 1038 passed, 2 skipped (3.13); 3.12 1033, 3.14 1039, 3.11 pure 293; 3.15 1039 with the pre-existing macOS sys.remote_exec PermissionError; cargo 9 tests; every reverted fix caught.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Every sync checks the key ending each dict; one forward scan, capped at the part the walker last saw, stops after its last entry or before the first key it does not know; __class__ joins values._COPY_PROTOCOL. Tests: a removal with as many additions before any copy (36 params), the removed key or copy put back, Python entries after all the walker wrote, copy.replace through __class__.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Tenth adversarial review (BLUEPRINT: decisions the eleventh review forced) found no mirror defect in about 160k fuzz seeds. It confirmed one older code defect: a memo hit in _mapping called isinstance on an entry Python code added, which reads that entry's __class__, so a mock or lazy proxy answering __class__ ran its code in the walker and again in the Python walk after the hand-back, and a stateful one changed the outcome. It also found two test gaps (unwritten rows only re-found the held copy; the precedence of the first unknown key was unpinned) and three doc inaccuracies. After the fixes: pytest 1054 passed, 2 skipped (3.13); 3.12 1049, 3.14 1055, 3.11 pure 293; 3.15 1055 with the pre-existing PermissionError; cargo 9 tests; 20/20 reverted fixes caught.
test_iterations.fix_applied: mapping.rs decides by exact type: reads an exact placeholder, treats builtin scalars and containers as none, hands anything else back before running code. Tests: a memo entry answering its own __class__ (property, __getattribute__, plain and builtin controls; 12 params); the held rows now make a new copy after Python's change; the last entry put back among the first entries. BLUEPRINT: cost condition, 'as many entries as the walker last saw', the unnoticed-removal example, stale placeholders seen by lazy readers.

test_iterations.failures_summary: Reviews twelve to twenty-two (BLUEPRINT: decisions the twelfth to twenty-second reviews forced) found that a context the cyclic collector freed lost the copies its walker had yet to write; that before 3.14 a dying context's untracked dicts, and on every version a spent C stack, change what a walker can write when it goes; that the lazily written mirror lost or misordered entries after a write that failed, a removal it noticed, or a copy replaced in place; that a key whose comparison runs code could fail between taking Python's entries out and putting them back; and that callbacks inside an eager call changed the dicts after the call's sync. After the fixes: pytest 1126 passed, 7 skipped (3.13); 3.12 1121, 3.14 1127, 3.11 pure 293; 3.15 1127 with the pre-existing macOS task-port PermissionError in test_native_pid_capture_preserves_business_frame; cargo 9 tests; rustfmt, clippy and ruff clean.
test_iterations.fix_applied: Walker.release is the native finalizer and the only place a walker writes when it goes (release.rs); a release that writes only ctx.objects owes _sources the originals it left out (State::owed, in place or appended); flush.rs writes what is owed first, each original before its copy, clears its notes only once all of it is written, puts Python's later entries back though a write fails, leaves them in place where a key may compare with code, and reads every key where a removal or a foreign key means it has not read them all; an eager commit checks the dicts again. Each code fix has a regression test in test_native_parity.py and was reverted to check that a test fails without it.

parity_iterations.divergence_cause: Seeds 13, 103, 143 (near-recursion-limit cases): State::enter only read the Python depth after 32 walk frames, so a call starting within CHECK_FROM+MARGIN (96) frames of the limit completed natively where the Python walk overflows (RecursionError or 'recursion' placeholders). handbacks == 0 on all three.
parity_iterations.fix_applied: Each transaction probes sys._getframe(limit - 97): ValueError proves the caller is far from the limit; otherwise the exact depth is read and checked on every enter. A RecursionError while probing hands the call straight back.

parity_iterations.divergence_cause: None: pickle.dumps byte-identical (epsilon 0) for 5000 random value-graph seeds x PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/12345 plus 20 end-to-end dumps each; deep/cyclic list/dict/object nesting past the recursion limit: 0 divergences.

Before the fixes, review reproducers diverged in application hooks (items() and __radd__ run twice through hand-backs), in results after __bases__ changes, and crashed on 64 KiB thread stacks. After: 5000 walk + 20 dump seeds x PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/2 on CPython 3.13 and once each on 3.14 and 3.15 byte-identical; every reviewer reproducer (stale bases, hand-back hooks, eager type info, exotic values, bytes identity, priority generators, class-level calls, overrides, reload, lifecycle) reports SAME; deep/cyclic near-limit check 0 divergences.
parity_iterations.fix_applied: See test iteration 4. On 3.15 the parity harness lifts the int string-digit limit so messages hold no addresses, and frozendict keys use hashable values.

parity_iterations.divergence_cause: None in the seeded sweep (5000 seeds x PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13, plus 3.14 and 3.15). Reproducer-only divergences fixed: walker drop and move between contexts, class-level call over a lazily mirrored memo.
parity_iterations.fix_applied: Flush into the previously mirrored dicts before switching; Drop refcount baseline; class attribute keeps routing to the walker.

parity_iterations.divergence_cause: Before the fixes the round-7 reproducers h1-h4 diverged (stale copy or original after a removal inside a hand-back, removed original kept alive, wrong object at a reused id), as did 7 copy-hook routes and 7 colliding-key hook counts. After: 30,000 parity seeds (5000 x PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13, 5000 on 3.14 and 3.15) and 24,000 mirror fuzz seeds (fuzz2 18,000, fuzz3 6,000) byte-identical; the remaining h5 (exception() then a removal) and patched Counter methods are documented differences.

Before the fixes the round-8 reproducers (flush past a moved boundary, a colliding _sources key's __eq__, copy.replace through __replace__) diverged, and the new mixing fuzzer found misordered unwritten copies after removals (both dicts, a re-added boundary, a non-id objects key). After: 30,000 parity seeds (5000 x PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13, 5000 on 3.14 and 3.15), 15,500 mixing-fuzzer seeds and 6,500 fuzz2/3/4 seeds byte-identical. Mixing-fuzzer cases left out as documented differences: equal-count removal and addition before any copy, an entry the walker wrote last put back in place, and an entry Python wrote for an unwritten copy and removed before the next call.

Before the fixes the ninth review's reproducers (count-neutral swap before a copy, last entry put back after an addition, copy.replace through __class__) diverged, and the unpadded mixing fuzzer found a known original in a replaced _sources counted as the walker's. After: 30,000 parity seeds (5000 x PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13, 5000 on 3.14 and 3.15) and 46,000 mirror fuzz seeds byte-identical but for documented differences (a non-id _sources key in an aliased dict, a put-back entry that stayed in place, a non-id key ahead).

Before the fix the planted-__class__ reproducer ran the hook twice natively and, for a stateful hook, changed truncation and node counts. After: 30,000 parity seeds (5000 x PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13, 5000 on 3.14 and 3.15) and 13,000 new mirror fuzz seeds byte-identical but for the same documented differences.
None in the final sweep: 5000 seeds for each PYTHONHASHSEED 0-3 on 3.13 and 5000 each on 3.14 and 3.15, byte-identical but for the documented differences.

benchmarks.label: Pure-Python walk (frozen pre-change package)
benchmarks.notes: Sum of per-workload median save_dumping times over 6 workloads, 3 rounds x >=15 runs, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, CPython 3.13.18, Apple M5 Pro; capture-only sum 73.220 ms; round spread 8.4%.

benchmarks.label: Safe Rust PyO3 walker (release, fat LTO, codegen-units=1)
benchmarks.notes: Save sum 2.91x (geomean 2.11x), capture sum 10.429 ms = 7.02x (geomean 3.64x) over legacy; byte-identical pickles, nodes and truncation on all 6 workloads; round spread 3.2%.

benchmarks.label: Layout pass: address-hashed maps, presized selection, entry API (no SIMD target)
benchmarks.notes: Over safe_rust: save sum 1.01x, capture sum 1.05x (round spread 5.9%, so within noise). No SIMD: the walk chases pointers through Python objects. Over legacy: save 2.93x, capture 7.35x; byte-identical snapshots.

benchmarks.label: PGO (train: 6 bench workloads x40 + native parity suite) + fat LTO
benchmarks.notes: Capture sum 9.291 ms = 7.88x over legacy (geomean 3.94x), +7% over the layout pass; save sum 2.91x (unchanged: pickling and file writes in Python dominate); round spread 1.5%; byte-identical snapshots. Per call: int 267 ns vs pure 91 ns (fixed transaction cost), list of 3 331 vs 1133 ns, dict of 5 1085 vs 4984 ns.

spotlight.explanation: The memo check at the top of _mapping. In Python, reading a cached placeholder's reason is an attribute lookup, and for an application's TruncatedValue subclass, or an instance dict with a key that collides with 'reason', that lookup runs application code. The Rust port answers natively only for an exact placeholder with a plain-keyed dict, and otherwise returns Halt::Bail: the whole call is rolled back and handed to the Python walk before any application code runs, so hooks run exactly as often as without the extension and the pickle stays byte-identical.
